---
title: "Installation"
---

phit is a PHP extension. It is installed into PHP itself, once per PHP
installation, rather than into a project with Composer. Projects that cannot
install extensions can use the [polyfill](extension-or-polyfill.qmd) instead.

## Requirements

- PHP 8.3, 8.4 or 8.5, non-thread-safe (NTS). Thread-safe (ZTS) builds are
  not supported.
- Linux or macOS. Windows is not supported.
- [PIE](https://github.com/php/pie), PHP's extension installer.
- `unzip`, or PHP's zip extension, for PIE to unpack a prebuilt binary.

## Install with PIE

```sh
pie install phpstats/phit
```

PIE finds the latest release on Packagist, installs `phit.so` into the
extension directory, and enables it for the PHP it runs under. To choose
another PHP installation, pass `--with-php-config=/path/to/php-config`.

On Linux x86_64 and arm64 with glibc 2.35 or later, PIE downloads a prebuilt
binary from the release, so nothing is compiled. Installing v0.3.1 this way
was tested in the official `php:8.4-cli-bookworm` image with PIE 1.5.0 and
`unzip`, and no Rust toolchain. The release workflow repeats the test for PHP
8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 on both architectures.

## Building from source

On macOS, and on Linux systems without a matching binary (Alpine and other
musl systems, or glibc older than 2.35), PIE builds the extension from
source. The build needs:

- PHP's development files: `phpize` and `php-config` for the same PHP
  installation.
- A C toolchain with `autoconf` and `make`.
- Rust, stable, from [rustup](https://rustup.rs).
- Clang and libclang.

These build tools are not needed at runtime.

On Debian or Ubuntu, the build tools come from:

```sh
sudo apt-get install build-essential autoconf pkg-config clang libclang-dev php-dev
curl -fsSL https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y
```

A source build of v0.3.0 was tested in the official `php:8.4-cli-bookworm`
image with PIE 1.5.0 and stable Rust. The image provides PHP's development
files, and the test added Clang, libclang and the image's `$PHPIZE_DEPS`.

On macOS, install the Xcode command-line tools (`xcode-select --install`),
Rust from rustup, and PHP and autoconf from Homebrew (`brew install php
autoconf`). `pie build phpstats/phit` completed for v0.3.0 on macOS 27 (Apple
silicon) with Homebrew PHP 8.5. If the build cannot find libclang, the
[development guide](development.qmd#environment) shows the variables that
select Homebrew's LLVM.

## Prebuilt Linux binaries

Each [GitHub release](https://github.com/phpstats/phit/releases) has the
binaries PIE uses, built and tested on Debian Bookworm for NTS, non-debug
PHP. They can also be installed by hand:

| PHP | x86_64 | arm64 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8.3 | `php_phit-v0.3.1_php8.3-x86_64-linux-glibc-nts.zip` | `php_phit-v0.3.1_php8.3-arm64-linux-glibc-nts.zip` |
| 8.4 | `php_phit-v0.3.1_php8.4-x86_64-linux-glibc-nts.zip` | `php_phit-v0.3.1_php8.4-arm64-linux-glibc-nts.zip` |
| 8.5 | `php_phit-v0.3.1_php8.5-x86_64-linux-glibc-nts.zip` | `php_phit-v0.3.1_php8.5-arm64-linux-glibc-nts.zip` |

Each archive holds `phit.so`, `INSTALL.txt`, a `manifest.json` that records
the build environment and the minimum glibc, the license, and the third-party
notices. A `.sha256` file sits beside each archive.

```sh
sha256sum -c php_phit-v0.3.1_php8.4-x86_64-linux-glibc-nts.sha256
unzip php_phit-v0.3.1_php8.4-x86_64-linux-glibc-nts.zip -d phit
sudo cp phit/phit.so "$(php-config --extension-dir)/"
```

Then add `extension=phit.so` to the PHP configuration for each runtime that
needs it, and restart PHP-FPM. The release workflow tests these steps for
every archive in the matching official PHP image. Releases up to v0.3.0 used
`.tar.gz` archives named `phit-0.3.0-php8.4-x86_64-nts-bookworm.tar.gz`,
which PIE does not download.

## Verify

```sh
php -r 'echo phpversion("phit"), PHP_EOL;'
```

```
0.3.1
```

The command line and PHP-FPM often read different configuration files. Check
the web runtime separately, for example with `extension_loaded('phit')` in a
request, and restart PHP-FPM workers after installing or upgrading.
[Deploying to servers](deployment.qmd) covers containers and FPM.

## Declare the dependency

An application can declare the extension in its composer.json, so Composer
reports a missing extension at install time:

```json
{
    "require": {
        "ext-phit": "*"
    }
}
```

The polyfill also satisfies `ext-phit`. See [Extension or
polyfill](extension-or-polyfill.qmd).

## Upgrade

Run `pie install phpstats/phit` again, or replace `phit.so` with the newer
binary, then restart PHP-FPM. The [release notes](https://github.com/phpstats/phit/releases)
describe each release.
